rfm_tuples.R: Our cash, cash equivalents and investment securities, as well as funds generated by anticipated sales of our products, will be sufficient to fund our planned operations through and beyond the next 12 months.
rfm_tuples.f: going_concern_detector + audit-opinion + balance-sheet check: scan 10-K for going-concern language, confirm auditor (E&Y) issued unqualified opinion, verify cash balance.
rfm_tuples.M_value: NO_GOING_CONCERN flag (n_matches=0); E&Y unqualified opinion 2/27/2025; auditor since 2015 with no resignations/disagreements; $328.4M cash+restricted at YE2024, $681.6M total cash+investments at 3/31/2025; YE2024 income from ops $230.8M; no debt/credit facility.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Balance sheet claim is well supported. Profitable on GAAP basis, no debt, ~2 years of runway at YE2024 burn pace (and FY2024 actually generated $157.7M operating cash flow). No covenant or going-concern issues.

rfm_tuples.R: Total operating expenses 727,003 ... Income (loss) from operations 230,794 ... Gain on sale of non-financial asset (146,515).
rfm_tuples.f: self_text MD&A — verify whether the FY2024 GAAP profit is recurring or one-time. Identify the gain on sale composition and recompute operating income ex-PRV.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K Consolidated Statements of Operations + MD&A)
rfm_tuples.M_value: $146.5M of the $230.8M operating income (63%) is from a one-time December 2024 sale of the Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher (PRV) to a third party for $150M gross (Neuren got 1/3 net per the license). Ex-PRV, true 2024 operating income is ~$84.3M on $957.8M revenue (~8.8% margin) and net cash from operations was $157.7M including PRV proceeds. The PRV cannot be sold again.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: FY2024 GAAP profitability is structurally overstated by a one-shot PRV sale. The headline 'income from operations $230.8M' obscures a ~$84M run-rate. Disclosed (PASS on existence) but the optics of 'profitable biotech' lean on a non-recurring asset disposal.

rfm_tuples.R: Net product sales from these two commercial products totaled $957.8 million for 2024, compared with $726.4 million for 2023. DAYBUE net revenue $348.4M (2024) vs $177.2M (2023).
rfm_tuples.f: claim_evolution + Q1 2025 10-Q MD&A comparison: verify DAYBUE growth trajectory is durable into Q1 2025 vs reported 2024 doubling.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2025 DAYBUE $84.6M vs Q1 2024 $75.9M = +11.5% YoY. Deceleration from FY2024's +96.6% YoY DAYBUE growth. NUPLAZID Q1 2025 $159.7M vs Q1 2024 $129.9M = +22.9% (vs FY24 NUPLAZID +10.9%). Both products still growing but DAYBUE growth rate has collapsed to ~12% annualized, well below the trajectory implied by FY2024's print.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: DAYBUE was the growth story driving the bull thesis; Q1 2025 (pre-cutoff) already shows persistence/new-start exhaustion. The 10-K's emphasis on 'drive new patient adoption' coincides with a sharp YoY slowdown — a Mode B mismatch between narrative intensity and disclosed run-rate.

rfm_tuples.R: Four of such customers, each based in the United States, accounted for approximately 73% of our NUPLAZID product revenue and 48% of our total product revenue ... Customer A 34% (2024) 23% (2023) *(2022) ... top five customers represent 83% of consolidated gross revenues.
rfm_tuples.f: self_text customer-concentration table — verify magnitude and stability of top-customer dependence.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Top customer (Customer A) jumped from <10% in 2022 to 23% in 2023 to 34% in 2024 — and 42% of AR at YE2024 (vs 33% YE2023). Top 5 customers = 83% of gross revenue (34+14+13+12+10). Disclosed in financial-statement notes but the magnitude of Customer A's escalation is not highlighted in MD&A.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosure exists (PASS on existence), but the concentration is severe and worsening: a single specialty pharmacy/distributor going through 34% of revenue and 42% of receivables creates material counterparty/payment-terms risk that is not foregrounded. Most biotech peers run 15-25% top-customer.

rfm_tuples.R: The composition of matter patent covering pimavanserin and salts thereof currently has an expiration date in 2030, including a patent term extension ... The patents covering the polymorph form and the use of pimavanserin or NUPLAZID for our approved indication are currently set to expire between 2024 and 2028.
rfm_tuples.f: self_text + openfda Orange Book + Hatch-Waxman/ANDA docket: assess generic exposure timeline for NUPLAZID, which is ~64% of FY2024 revenue.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K Patents section) + openFDA approved drugs registry
rfm_tuples.M_value: NUPLAZID composition-of-matter patent expires 2030 (5 years from cutoff); polymorph/use patents already expiring 2024-2028. Hetero settled to launch generic Feb 27, 2038 (favorable, contingent triggers). Aurobindo/MSN/Zydus ANDA litigation pending. openFDA confirms NUPLAZID 207318 + 210793 with Pimavanserin Tartrate active ingredient. The 2038 settlement is contingent on triggers; if any other generic launches first, Hetero accelerates.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosed honestly. But ~64% of revenue rides on a patent estate where the composition-of-matter cliff is 2030 and at least three ANDA cases (Aurobindo, MSN, Zydus) are unresolved. NUPLAZID growth has to compress materially within ~5 years of cutoff. Hetero 2038 settlement is good news with conditions; not addressing it as a remaining risk is a mild Mode B gap.

rfm_tuples.R: In March 2024 we reported top-line results from a Phase 3 study of pimavanserin for the treatment of the negative symptoms of schizophrenia. Pimavanserin did not demonstrate a statistically significant improvement over placebo on the study's primary endpoint.
rfm_tuples.f: self_text + clinical_trials registry — verify lifecycle failure count for pimavanserin and what remains in the actively-developed pipeline.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K & 10-Q Risk Factors) + clinical_trials.gov via m_sources.clinical_trials
rfm_tuples.M_value: Pimavanserin failures: Phase 3 negative-symptoms schizophrenia (ADVANCE-2, March 2024) FAILED; Phase 2 autism irritability (October 2024) FAILED. ClinicalTrials.gov registry shows 9 of 38 Acadia studies pre-cutoff are TERMINATED (~24% termination rate). Only one product (DAYBUE) has been approved from pipeline development since NUPLAZID (2016). Active pipeline: ACP-101 Phase 3 PWS (read-out 1H 2026), ACP-204 Phase 2 ADP, ACP-711 Phase 1, ACP-2591 preclinical.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Honestly disclosed (PASS), but the implied claim that 'pimavanserin has lifecycle expansion potential' has been falsified by repeated trial failures. ~24% trial termination rate is elevated. Without a label expansion for NUPLAZID and with DAYBUE growth decelerating, near-term catalysts depend almost entirely on ACP-101 Phase 3 read-out — single-asset binary risk.

rfm_tuples.R: In September 2024, Catherine Owen Adams became our new Chief Executive Officer (CEO), replacing our former CEO, Stephen R. Davis. Our new CEO will be critical to executing on and achieving our strategy. Further, our new CEO may bring different perspectives, and the future strategy and direction of our business may evolve.
rfm_tuples.f: self_text + form4: verify CEO transition timing, severance footprint, and insider-selling cluster around the transition window.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K Risk Factors + Exhibit 10.10 Executive Transition Agreement dated 9/23/2024) + form4 / insider_vs_calendar
rfm_tuples.M_value: CEO Davis exit and Owen Adams arrival both effective Sept 23, 2024 (Exhibit 10.10 'Executive Transition Agreement' + Exhibit 10.12 new CEO Employment Agreement). 10-K Risk Factors explicitly hedges that 'future strategy and direction of our business may evolve.' Form 4 data: 52 Form 4 filings, 37 total insider sales over the 540-day lookback for total ~$3.36M — relatively modest aggregate sales; no large CEO/CFO discretionary block sale clustered to the transition window or near the PRV sale announcement.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: CEO transition disclosed and corroborated by Form 4 / exhibits. Insider selling magnitude is low and not clustered to capital events. The 'strategy may evolve' hedge is genuinely Mode A unverifiable forward-looking — but the small insider-sale footprint supports good faith.

rfm_tuples.R: In April 2021, a purported stockholder of us filed a putative securities class action complaint (captioned City of Birmingham Relief Retirement Systems v. Acadia Pharmaceuticals Inc., Case No. 21-cv-0762) ... against us and certain of our current executive officers.
rfm_tuples.f: edgar_fts / self_text: verify the case status, the period covered, and the underlying allegations to gauge tail litigation exposure.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Securities class action still pending pre-cutoff (filed April 19, 2021, S.D. Cal.). Underlying allegations concern NUPLAZID-related disclosures from a prior era; not dismissed. Plus active ANDA patent litigation against Aurobindo, MSN, Zydus (Zydus response due 4/29/2025). No reserve disclosed.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosed (PASS on existence), but ongoing securities-litigation exposure with no accrued loss is a contingent liability that the framework cannot size from filings alone. Standard pharma legal-tail risk; not framework-distinguishing.

rfm_tuples.R: Our strategy to drive sales growth for DAYBUE in the U.S. is to drive new patient adoption while optimizing the patient experience for those already on therapy thereby achieving and maintaining stable persistency rates. ... issues may arise with respect to patient acceptance, adherence, persistence and compliance rates.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B implied verification: if persistency were stable and new-patient additions strong, Q1 2025 DAYBUE revenue should be tracking the FY2024 doubling. Cross-check Q1 10-Q.
rfm_tuples.M_value: DAYBUE Q1 2025 $84.6M = +11.5% YoY (vs FY24 +96.6% YoY). Q1 2024 was $75.9M, Q4 2024 implied ~$87M (348.4 − (75.9+90+95)). So sequential growth from Q4 2024 to Q1 2025 is essentially flat-to-slightly down. The 10-K's 'stable persistency' claim is consistent with a saturated patient pool, not an expanding one. No disclosure of total patient count, prescriber count, or persistence rate.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B finding. Company doesn't quantify patient adds, persistence, or discontinuation rate. The flat-to-down sequential and the 11% YoY trajectory in Q1 are consistent with a small-population rare-disease drug at or near peak penetration of the disclosed 4,500-5,000 diagnosed Rett patients in the US. Not lying, but the growth narrative is structurally exhausted faster than the 10-K implies.

rfm_tuples.R: We expect to complete enrollment in our Phase 3 COMPASS PWS study in the fourth quarter of 2025 and subsequently report top-line results sometime in the first half of 2026. In the event of positive trial results, we believe ACP-101 has the potential for FDA approval in the fourth quarter of 2026.
rfm_tuples.f: clinical_trials registry: verify NCT for COMPASS PWS, status and enrollment posture pre-cutoff.
rfm_tuples.M_value: ClinicalTrials registry confirms ACP-101 PWS Phase 3 study active; OLE study NCT06420297 ENROLLING_BY_INVITATION started 3/11/2024. Registry pre-cutoff status RECRUITING for the main study consistent with Q4 2025 enrollment completion guidance. No registry-level slippage signal detected pre-cutoff.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A verifiable: the lead pipeline catalyst is registered, on its disclosed timeline, with an OLE running. Single-asset binary risk remains, but the operational claim verifies.

deterministic_flags.one_time_gain_pct_of_opinc: 63.5% of FY2024 operating income is one-time PRV sale

summary: ACAD is an honest, fully-disclosing mid-cap biotech with a clean balance sheet (~$682M cash, no debt), unqualified E&Y opinion since 2015, and no going-concern or covenant issues. The framework's main findings are Mode B: (1) FY2024 GAAP profit is ~63% from a one-time PRV sale and run-rate operating income is closer to $84M; (2) DAYBUE growth has decelerated sharply from ~+97% YoY in 2024 to ~+12% YoY in Q1 2025 (sequentially flat), consistent with rare-disease patient-pool saturation that the 'drive new patient adoption' narrative obscures; (3) top customer concentration escalated from <10% to 34% of revenue and 42% of AR over two years; (4) NUPLAZID (~64% of revenue) has a 2030 composition-of-matter patent cliff with multiple unresolved ANDAs; (5) two pimavanserin trial failures in 2024 leave a single-asset binary (ACP-101 Phase 3 read-out 1H 2026) as the next material catalyst. Not lying, but the headline 'profitable, growing biotech' framing is structurally weaker than presented. Verdict: NEUTRAL with a SHORT-tilt — the honesty filter does not exclude it, but earnings quality and growth trajectory are deteriorating.
